The Resolution That the Search Is Given, Out of the Readings Taken So Far

Source: R/outer_context.R
resolution_summary.Rd

Returns the largest of the usable readings that criterion_resolution() has returned during this search.

Usage

resolution_summary(x)

Arguments

x

Every usable reading so far.

Value

A single positive number, or NA_real_ where there is none.

Details

A reading is taken at every usable evaluation, and each one measures how far the criterion moves when the mode is displaced by the error at which that evaluation's inner fit stopped. The displacement varies across evaluations by far more than the quantity that it represents does, so the answer depends on which reading is kept.

The readings are already filtered to acceptable modes, because criterion_resolution() returns NA where the mode error exceeds mode_error_limit(), so every reading that reaches this function comes from a mode that the layer accepts. The largest of them is therefore the one to keep. A resolution has to bound how far the criterion can move between two such modes, and not how little it moved at the evaluation whose inner score happened to stop lowest.

The inner score at which a Newton step stops varies by orders of magnitude across evaluations, and a minimum over such a sequence reads the luckiest one, which understates the resolution. A resolution far below the true one leaves the line search backtracking for improvements that the criterion cannot resolve, and the run ends by exhausting outer_backtracks() and not on a stopping rule.

See also

criterion_resolution(), outer_fit()
